title: The tavern on Wells and owner Demling
summary: The first Chicago tavern the band played, a profitable job where tips were stolen.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Really? Mr. Tavern? Yeah, it was a tavern. Oh man, that place was like the idea of a band from York. That man made money, I mean he made money, hand over fist. He wanted to keep us, but I don't know, it seemed like them fellas that he had, you know, working there, them guys, they would take the tips. A lot of them guys would steal the tips, you know, and what a little snotty thing, a man handed a dollar and he'd stick it in his pocket, you know. He didn't want us to leave though, he wanted us to, I think his name was Demling. What is that, is that Irish or sweet? Demling. Sounds more like Irish, I guess. Yeah, Demling, that was the guy's name. And he didn't want us to leave, he wanted to keep us over there, but the boys all got married, we can't make no money. Yeah. So we left.
